articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 vulns including a SharePoint zero-day and a Windows Defender flaw dubbed 'BlueHammer' — because apparently someone thought Defender needed more ways to fail. Chrome patches its fourth of the year because Google's security model is 'move fast and break browsers.'

articles.title: Hackers Use AI for Exploit Development, Attack Automation
articles.summary: 'Dirty Frag' joins the Linux privilege escalation hall of fame alongside Copy Fail and Dirty Pipe. Enterprise distros are about to get fragged, and there's whispers it's already happening in the wild.

articles.title: Big Finance Might Be Dooming the SPLC — Even Before Its Day in Court
articles.summary: Trump's DOJ now treats dodging FOIA requests as a criminal offense worthy of arrest and strip searches — the irony of transparency-dodgers criminalizing transparency-dodging is chef's kiss perfection. Rules for thee, surveillance for me.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Linux Rootkit, macOS Crypto Stealer, WebSocket Skimmers and More
articles.summary: Google confirms the first AI-developed zero-day used in the wild — a 2FA bypass for mass exploitation. The machines aren't just coming for our jobs, they're coming for our security too.

articles.title: Native Apps Should Be Avoided Whenever Possible
articles.summary: LLMs have murdered the 90-day disclosure window by compressing both bug discovery and exploit development to near-zero timelines. The responsible disclosure era just got machine-gunned by artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: ShinyHunters ransoms Canvas, disrupting millions of students during finals week because apparently psychological warfare against sleep-deprived college kids is their new business model. Educational technology meets educational terrorism.

articles.title: Hackers Used AI to Develop First Known Zero-Day 2FA Bypass for Mass Exploitation
articles.summary: CVE-2026-41940 in cPanel gets weaponized by 'Mr_Rot13' to deploy Filemanager backdoors — because nothing says 'elite hacker' like a Caesar cipher username and targeting shared hosting providers. Script kiddie energy meets critical infrastructure.

articles.title: EFF Stands in Solidarity With RightsCon and the Global Digital Rights Community
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence units are mass-harvesting Microsoft Office tokens through compromised routers like it's 2003 and we learned nothing. State-sponsored credential theft via neglected network hardware — the classics never die.

articles.title: Congress Narrowed the GUARD Act, But Serious Problems Remain
articles.summary: RightsCon 2026 gets cancelled as governments worldwide crush spaces for digital rights dialogue. When they're shutting down the conferences about digital freedom, maybe it's time to worry about digital freedom.

articles.title: Milestone 1.0.0 Release of APK Downloader `apkeep` Powers Research on Android Apps
articles.summary: EFF drops a free Signal guide in Spanish and English because encrypted messaging shouldn't require a computer science degree. Guy Kawasaki's 'Everybody Has Something to Hide' — finally, a privacy advocate who gets the marketing game.
